newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo consumer defaults jump 65 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo consumer defaults jump 65 pct in March.

text.p: Consumer defaults in Sao Paulo city jumped 65 percent year-on-year to a record 275,915 in March, said the Sao Paulo Commerce Association (ACSP).

March consumer debt defaults, which are measured by the number of reported payments in arrears for over 30 days, were the highest since April 1995, when consumer defaults totalled 245,494, ACSP president Elvio Aliprandi said.
In the first quarter of the year, consumer defaults soared 55.4 percent to 638,583, he said.
Aliprandi said debt default growth in the first quarter and in March were higher than the growth in sales, noting that it was above the market's expectation. "However, it is not explosive," he said.

The growth in consumer defaults was a result of an increase in sales on credit and unemployment, he said. Despite the rise of consumer defaults, Aliprandi said there was a drop in bankruptcies and debt relief filings in March.
Bankruptcy filings in the city of Sao Paulo totalled 948 in March, a drop of 34.8 percent over the same month last year but up 3.9 percent on February.
In addition, 10 Sao Paulo firms filed for debt relief last month against 32 in March 1996. March debt relief filings remained unchanged when compared to February.
